name: Pop Culture APIs
description: Practice data manipulation with fun, deeply nested datasets inspired by real API response shapes. Each theme features punny parody names and rich data structures that drill chained iterator methods, bracket notation, and complex transformations.
attribution: Original exercises with fictional parody datasets inspired by public API response shapes. All character names and data are humorous parodies for educational purposes.

exercises.title: Movies: Get All Titles
exercises.description: Extract all movie titles from the dataset using the map method.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getAllTitles` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of their titles.

Each movie object has a `title` property (string).

Example:
```
getAllTitles(movies)
// Returns: ["The Shawshank Exemption", "The Codfather", ...]
```

exercises.title: Movies: Filter by Genre
exercises.description: Filter movies that belong to a specific genre.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `filterByGenre` that takes an array of movie objects and a genre string, and returns an array of movies whose `genres` array includes that genre.

Each movie has a `genres` property which is an array of strings.

Example:
```
filterByGenre(movies, "horror")
// Returns: [{ title: "The Silence of the Clams", ... }, { title: "The Whining", ... }]
```

exercises.title: Movies: Get Director Names
exercises.description: Extract director names from nested movie objects using dot notation.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getDirectorNames` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of director name strings.

Each movie has a `director` property which is an object with a `name` property.

Example:
```
getDirectorNames(movies)
// Returns: ["Frank Darabonk", "Francis Ford Cappuccino", ...]
```

exercises.description: Filter movies released within a given year range.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `filterByYearRange` that takes an array of movie objects, a `startYear`, and an `endYear`, and returns movies released between those years (inclusive).

Example:
```
filterByYearRange(movies, 1990, 1994)
// Returns movies from 1990, 1991, 1993, and 1994
```

```
sortByYear(movies)

```

exercises.title: Movies: All Cast Members
exercises.description: Extract all unique cast member names from every movie.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `allCastMembers` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of unique cast member names across all movies.

Each movie has a `cast` array of objects, each with a `name` property. Some actors may appear in multiple movies.

Example:
```
allCastMembers(movies)
// Returns: ["Tim Bobbins", "Morgan Freebird", "Marlon Branflakes", ...]
```

exercises.title: Movies: Most Profitable
exercises.description: Find profitable movies and rank them by profit margin.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `mostProfitable` that takes an array of movie objects and returns an array of `{ title, profit, roi }` objects for movies where total revenue (domestic + international) exceeded the budget. Sort by `roi` (return on investment) in descending order.

- `profit` = (domestic + international) - budget
- `roi` = profit / budget, rounded to 1 decimal

Example:
```
mostProfitable(movies)
// Returns: [{ title: "The Codfather", profit: 238966411, roi: 39.8 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Get Artist Names
exercises.description: Extract all artist names from the dataset using the map method.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getArtistNames` that takes an array of artist objects and returns an array of their names.

Each artist has a `name` property (string).

Example:
```
getArtistNames(artists)
// Returns: ["Bad Bunion", "Taylor Drift", ...]
```

exercises.description: Extract origin city and country from nested artist objects.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getOrigins` that takes an array of artist objects and returns an array of strings in the format `"City, Country"`.

Each artist has an `origin` property which is an object with `city` and `country`.

Example:
```
getOrigins(artists)
// Returns: ["San Huan, Puerto Rico", "West Reeding, USA", ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Artist Grammy Summary
exercises.description: Build summary objects with artist names and Grammy stats.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `grammySummary` that takes an array of artist objects and returns an array of objects with:
- `name`: the artist's name
- `wins`: their Grammy wins
- `nominations`: their Grammy nominations
- `winRate`: wins divided by nominations, rounded to 2 decimal places (or 0 if no nominations)

Example:
```
grammySummary(artists)
// Returns: [{ name: "Bad Bunion", wins: 3, nominations: 18, winRate: 0.17 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Albums for Artist
exercises.description: Find all albums belonging to a specific artist using cross-referencing.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getArtistAlbums` that takes the `artists` array, the `albums` array, and an artist name string. It should find the artist by name, then return all albums whose `artistId` matches that artist's `id`.

Return an empty array if the artist is not found.

Example:
```
getArtistAlbums(artists, albums, "Billie Eyelash")
// Returns: [{ title: "HIT ME HARD AND GENTLY", ... }, { title: "When We All Fall Asleep...", ... }]
```

Write a function called `totalTracks` that takes an array of album objects and returns the total number of tracks across all albums.

Example:
```
totalTracks(albums) // Returns: 94
```


exercises.title: Music: Featured Artists
exercises.description: Extract all unique featured artist names from album tracks.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getFeaturedArtists` that takes an array of album objects and returns an array of unique artist names that appear as features on any track.

Each track has a `features` array of artist name strings (may be empty).

Example:
```
getFeaturedArtists(albums)
// Returns: ["Quake", "Fuerza Refrita", "The Weeknight", ...]
```

exercises.title: Music: Artist Discography Report
exercises.description: Build a discography report for each artist by cross-referencing both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `discographyReport` that takes the `artists` and `albums` arrays and returns an array of objects, one per artist, with:
- `name`: artist name
- `albumCount`: number of albums
- `totalTracks`: total tracks across all their albums
- `totalSales`: sum of `certification.sales` across all their albums
- `topAlbum`: title of their album with the highest `ratings.fan` score

Sort the result by `totalSales` descending.

Example:
```
discographyReport(artists, albums)
// Returns: [{ name: "Bad Bunion", albumCount: 2, totalTracks: 11, totalSales: 11700000, topAlbum: "Un Verano Sin WiFi" }, ...]
```

hints: Process in two passes: first loop through artists to populate each label with its artist names, then loop through albums to add album counts and sales.
Use an object as an accumulator. For each label, track unique artists (check with .includes()), and count albums separately using album.label.

exercises.title: Music: Full Streaming Analysis
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive streaming platform analysis from both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `streamingAnalysis` that takes the `artists` and `albums` arrays and returns an object with:
- `totalArtists`: number of artists
- `totalAlbums`: number of albums
- `totalTracks`: total tracks across all albums
- `avgListeners`: average monthlyListeners across all artists (rounded to nearest integer)
- `mostGrammys`: `{ name, wins }` of the artist with the most Grammy wins
- `highestRated`: `{ title, artist, fan }` of the album with the highest fan rating (include the artist name by looking up artistId)
- `certificationCounts`: object mapping certification status to count of albums (e.g., `{ diamond: 4, platinum: 10, gold: 4 }`)

Example:
```
streamingAnalysis(artists, albums)
// Returns: { totalArtists: 10, totalAlbums: 18, ... }
```

Each game has a `title` property (string).

Example:
```
getGameTitles(games)
// Returns: ["Clair Absurd: Expedition 33⅓", "Balder's Gate 3", ...]
```

```
gamesSince(games, 2023)
// Returns games from 2023, 2024, and 2025
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Platforms for Game
exercises.description: Find all platform names a specific game is available on using cross-referencing.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getGamePlatforms` that takes the `platforms` array, the `games` array, and a game title string. It should find the game by title, then return an array of platform name strings by matching the game's `platformIds` against platform `id` values.

Return an empty array if the game is not found.

Example:
```
getGamePlatforms(platforms, games, "Astro Botch")
// Returns: ["GameStation 5"]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Unique Genres
exercises.description: Extract all unique genres from across all games.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `getUniqueGenres` that takes an array of game objects and returns a sorted array of all unique genre strings found across all games.

Each game has a `genres` array.

Example:
```
getUniqueGenres(games)
// Returns: ["action", "adventure", "battle-royale", ...]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Sort by Playtime
exercises.description: Sort games by completionist playtime, excluding games without playtime data.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `sortByPlaytime` that takes an array of game objects and returns an array of objects with `title` and `completionist` properties, sorted from longest to shortest completionist playtime.

Exclude games where `playtime.completionist` is `null`.

Example:
```
sortByPlaytime(games)
// Returns: [{ title: "Mineshaft", completionist: 420 }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Platform Library Report
exercises.description: Build a library report for each platform showing its games and player stats.
exercises.instructions:
Write a function called `platformReport` that takes the `platforms` and `games` arrays and returns an array of objects, one per platform, with:
- `name`: platform name
- `gameCount`: number of games available on that platform
- `totalPlayers`: sum of `players.total` across games on that platform
- `topGame`: title of the game on that platform with the highest `ratings.metacritic`
- `exclusiveCount`: number of games ONLY on that platform

Sort by `gameCount` descending.

Example:
```
platformReport(platforms, games)
// Returns: [{ name: "GameStation 5", gameCount: 10, ... }, ...]
```

exercises.title: Video Games: Full Gaming Analysis
exercises.description: Build a comprehensive gaming industry analysis from both datasets.
exercises.instructions:
Create a function called `gamingAnalysis` that takes the `platforms` and `games` arrays and returns an object with:
- `totalGames`: number of games
- `totalPlatforms`: number of platforms
- `totalPlayers`: sum of all `players.total`
- `avgMetacritic`: average Metacritic across all games (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `mostAwarded`: `{ title, totalAwards }` of the game with the most total awards (sum of gameAwards + bafta + diceAwards)
- `mostPopular`: `{ title, players }` of the game with highest `players.total`
- `manufacturerBreakdown`: object mapping each platform manufacturer to `{ platforms, totalGamesSold }` where `platforms` is an array of platform names and `totalGamesSold` is the sum of `unitsSold` (skip null values)

Example:
```
gamingAnalysis(platforms, games)
// Returns: { totalGames: 12, totalPlatforms: 6, ... }
```
